title: Los Angeles weather: Storm expected to bring heavy rain, flood risk to Southern California. Here's the timeline - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Storm expected to bring heavy rain, flood risk to Southern California. Here's the timeline - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 Storm expected to bring heavy rain, flood risk to SoCal. Here's the timeline 
 Wednesday, November 18, 2026 5:12AM 
 Este artículo se ofrece en Español Southern California is bracing for another storm that could bring the potential for heavy rainfall and flooding. LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Southern California is bracing for another storm that could bring the potential for heavy rainfall and flooding.
 Wednesday is expected to remain dry during the day, with mild temperatures across much of the region. However, conditions start changing as the storm moves in overnight, with the heaviest rain hitting the region Thursday morning. ABC7 has issued a Weather Change Alert for Thursday.
 Current estimates indicate heavier rain could reach Los Angeles County during the Thursday morning rush hour, impacting drivers on the roads. The storm is expected to move out relatively quickly, though showers could linger into Friday.
 Some areas could receive between 1 and 4 inches of rain, while strong winds are also expected.
 High surf advisories are expected to expire early Wednesday morning. Meanwhile, Ventura County and much of Los Angeles County will be under a flood watch Thursday due to the anticipated rainfall.
 Wednesday forecast
 Los Angeles and Orange counties Wednesday can expect partly cloudy conditions, along with a high of 67 and a low of 54. On Thursday, expect rainfall totals between 1 and 2 inches.
 The valleys and Inland Empire Wednesday will see morning clouds, with a high of 67 degrees and a low of 51. Rainfall totals between 1 and 4 inches are possible Thursday.
 Beach communities on Wednesday can expect partly cloudy conditions, with a high of 71 and a low of 56. The storm could bring between 1 to 3 inches of rain Thursday.
 Mountain communities will be partly cloudy Wednesday, with a high of 48 degrees and a chilly overnight low of 21. Rainfall totals of 3 to 5 inches are possible Thursday, with snow falling at elevations above 7,500 feet.
 Desert areas can expect a high of 61 and a low of 37 on Wednesday, with Palm Springs reaching a high of 73. Up to 1 inch of rain is possible on Thursday.
